newsitem.title: BRAZIL: OLYMPICS-BRAZIL BACKS BUENOS AIRES, WILL TRY AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-BRAZIL BACKS BUENOS AIRES, WILL TRY AGAIN.

text.p: Brazil was graceful in defeat on Friday following the end of Rio de Janeiro's Olympic dream, promising to lend moral support to Buenos Aires and to bid again for the 2008 Olympics.

A country that is plunged into mourning when its national soccer team loses an important game greeted the International Olympic Comittee's decision to exclude Rio from the final shortlist of bidders with a mild sense of resignation.
Officially, Brazil accepted the verdict quietly and there was little of the bitterness demonstrated by some other defeated candidates.

President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said the government would maintain its commitments to invest in improving the city's infrastrasture despite Rio's failure to make the shortlist of five candidate cities.

"We will prepare Rio to be in a good position to have another go next time," he said. He spoke of the importance of having Mercosul -- a free market that includes Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay -- represented in the race.
Pele, the government's sports minister, said from Lausanne where he was part of the delegation: "The criteria is extremely thorough. We can't say it was an unfair decision."

Ronaldo Cezar Coelho, president of the Rio 2004 committee, said he would back Buenos Aires, which was included in the shortlist, despite the obvious rivalry between Brazil and Argentina. "We are not going to throw stones at our neighbour."
But the decision also brought a certain amount of embarrassment to both the committee and much of the media, which had set about convincing the population that Rio was a firm favourite.

The Rio delegation left the country for Lausanne on Monday exuding confidence after drawing tens of thousands of people to Copacabana beach on Sunday in a demonstration of popular support for the candidature.
An estimated half a million balloons were launched by the public and Coelho said: "No other candidate city has done anything like this."
Globo television, in its preview of the vote, told viewers that Rio had done better than Buenos Aires in the presentations made by candidate cities to the IOC on Thursday.
It said Rio got a standing ovation from delegates - - apparently referring to a speech made by Pele -- while the Argentine capital had exceeded the time limit.
While Brazil officially backed their neighbours, the public seemed less keen.
"We lost out to Buenos Aires," said one elderly lady in a television interview. "That's difficult to swallow."
